items.title: 2026-012: Critical Vulnerabilities in Check Point Products
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-012: Check Point released emergency updates for two critical flaws in Security Gateway, Security Management Server and Spark Firewall deployments using Remote Access or Site-to-Site VPN.

items.title: 2026-011: Critical Vulnerabilities in SAP Kernel and NetWeaver Message Server
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-011: SAP's September Patch Day fixes two critical flaws, the most severe CVE-2026-44756 (CVSS 10.0), a memory corruption issue in SAP Extended Password-related components affecting a broad product range.

items.title: 2026-010: Critical Vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway
items.summary: CERT-EU advisory 2026-010 covers multiple critical vulnerabilities in Citrix NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway; CERT-EU urges updating affected appliances as soon as possible.

items.title: Critical ScreenConnect flaw now actively exploited in attacks
items.summary: CISA reports active in-the-wild exploitation of a critical ConnectWise ScreenConnect vulnerability, putting remote access and RMM tooling back in the spotlight.

items.title: Kritische Sicherheitslücke in Cisco Secure Email Gateway - aktiv ausgenutzt - Updates verfügbar
items.summary: CERT.at warns of a critical, actively exploited vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway that could let unauthenticated remote attackers execute commands with root privileges; updates are available.

items.title: CVE-2026-76461: Critical Cisco Secure Email Gateway Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
items.summary: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76461, a critical SQL injection flaw (CVSS 9.8) in AsyncOS for Secure Email Gateway that unauthenticated attackers are exploiting in the wild, per Rapid7's analysis.

items.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch 115 Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Browser patch round: Google fixed 42 security defects in Chrome and Mozilla resolved 73 bugs in Firefox, 115 vulnerabilities in total. Endpoint fleets should roll updates promptly.

items.title: Securing the unpatchable in an age of AI-driven vulnerabilities
items.summary: Cisco Talos argues AI will keep surfacing vulnerabilities that are hard or impossible to patch, and recommends network segmentation, rigorous visibility and NGFW/IPS as compensating controls.

items.title: Atomic macOS (AMOS) Stealer Activity
items.summary: Unit 42 details ongoing Atomic macOS (AMOS) stealer activity, where deceptive setup guides trick users into handing over credentials and sensitive data, with detection and blocking guidance.

items.title: Acronis Patches Exploited Vulnerability in cPanel Backup Plugin
items.summary: Acronis patched CVE-2026-87886, a high-severity insecure file permissions flaw in its cPanel backup plugin that enables local privilege escalation and is reported as exploited.

items.title: Acronis backup plugin flaw exploited in targeted attacks (CVE-2026-87886)
items.summary: Acronis warns CVE-2026-87886, a Linux privilege escalation flaw in its backup extensions for cPanel, WHM and Plesk, is being exploited in targeted attacks in the wild.

items.title: Windows Server 2022 reaches end of mainstream support next month
items.summary: Microsoft reminds customers Windows Server 2022 reaches end of mainstream support next month and moves into extended support until October 2031, a lifecycle planning item for server estates.

items.title: Iranian hackers use CHOSEN BRICK data-stealing malware to spy on dissidents and journalists
items.summary: Three Western intelligence agencies, including the UK NCSC, warn Iranian state actors are deploying CHOSEN BRICK data-stealing malware against dissidents and journalists, reaching victims via messaging apps and infecting Windows devices.

items.title: US exposes alleged Russian terror network targeting Ukraine allies
items.summary: US prosecutors exposed an alleged Russian network that planned attacks on civilian and military infrastructure across Europe, targeting countries supporting Ukraine.

items.title: EU's von der Leyen calls for pacing frontier AI models
items.summary: In her State of the Union address, von der Leyen called for pacing the development of frontier AI models and pledged closer AI safety cooperation with Canada, the UK and other partners.

items.title: Iranian cyber targeting of dissidents, activists and journalists
items.summary: The UK NCSC published an advisory on CHOSEN BRICK malware, with technical analysis and protective advice for individuals and organisations at risk.

items.title: UK and allies expose spyware used by Iranian state actors to target dissidents, activists and journalists
items.summary: The UK and allied agencies publicly exposed spyware used by Iranian state actors against dissidents, activists and journalists, with detection and mitigation advice.

items.title: Ministry of Justice apologizes after court staff accessed Southport victims' files
items.summary: The UK Ministry of Justice apologised after court staff improperly accessed Southport victims' files containing sensitive personal data; no evidence of onward sharing has been found.

items.title: CenterPoint Energy confirms data breach following claims on hacking forum
items.summary: US utility CenterPoint Energy confirmed an unauthorised third party accessed customer data via an external system, after a hacking forum claim that millions of records were stolen.

items.title: One runaway AI agent racked up a $50,000 cloud bill
items.summary: Report on autonomous AI systems running API calls and production changes, including a runaway agent that generated a USD 50,000 cloud bill, alongside indirect prompt injection and AI supply chain risks.

items.title: Thousands of suspicious accounts followed Swedish political voices, researchers say
items.summary: Researchers identified more than 8,500 suspicious X accounts following Swedish political voices ahead of the general election, pointing to coordinated influence activity.

items.title: Von der Leyen pitches European Security Council in response to Trump and Putin
items.summary: The Commission president pitched a European Security Council in response to pressure from Washington and Moscow, citing the nature and scale of current risks.

items.title: EU digital wallet: 24 of 27 members will miss the deadline
items.summary: Only three of 27 EU member states have launched a digital ID wallet, so 24 are set to miss the 24 December 2026 deadline, a compliance gap for eIDAS-dependent services.

items.title: Tageszusammenfassung - 15.09.2026
items.summary: CERT.at's end-of-day report for 15 September 2026 covers current Austrian threat items, including multilingual phishing campaigns abusing the FinanzOnline tax portal brand.

items.title: Andorran Police joins Europol’s secure communication network
items.summary: The Andorran Police joined Europol's secure communication network under a Memorandum of Understanding, enabling secure law enforcement information sharing with European and international partners.

items.title: Crackdown on Italian organised criminal network involved in large-scale euro counterfeiting
items.summary: Europol supported an international operation against a Camorra-linked network involved in large-scale euro counterfeiting, coordinated by German police and the Stuttgart prosecutor's office.

items.title: EU chief backs plan for Canada to become 'associate member'
items.summary: The European Commission president backs a plan for Canada to become an EU 'associate member', as Ottawa seeks closer ties with Europe after strained relations with the US.

items.title: EU's Ursula von der Leyen says she wants Canada to become an associate member
items.summary: European Commission President von der Leyen proposed making Canada the EU's first associate member, an overture as US tariffs push Ottawa closer to Europe.

items.title: 280,000 Impacted by Premier Medical Group Data Breach
items.summary: Premier Medical Group says a June 2026 intrusion exposed files with patient names, contact details, diagnosis information and health insurance data, affecting about 280,000 people.

items.title: Poll: Americans say there’s a serious risk of AI destroying humanity
items.summary: A POLITICO poll finds a plurality of Americans favour pausing development of more advanced AI models, with 63 percent seeing at least moderate risk of AI destroying humanity.

items.title: EU capitals caught off guard as von der Leyen announces ‘associate membership’ for Canada
items.summary: EU capitals were caught off guard by von der Leyen's 'associate membership' offer to Canada; diplomats warn deeper alignment raises issues on steel, cars and GM crops.

items.title: OpenAI boss says world 'right to be afraid' but should trust AI firms
items.summary: OpenAI's chief executive said the world is 'right to be afraid' of AI but should trust AI firms, as tech CEOs argue there are incentives to limit advances amid growing safety concerns.

items.title: Kosovo ex-president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
items.summary: A Hague tribunal sentenced former Kosovo president Hashim Thaci to 25 years for war crimes committed during the independence war with Serbia.

items.title: At least five killed in Russian drone strike near Ukraine front line
items.summary: A Russian drone strike near Nikopol in south-eastern Ukraine killed at least five people and injured seven, the Dnipropetrovsk governor said.

items.title: China Isn’t Buying Silicon Valley’s Call for an AI Slowdown
items.summary: Analysis of why Beijing is sceptical of Silicon Valley's proposed AI slowdown: both the US and China acknowledge advanced AI risks, but China resists a deal seen as locking in US leadership.

items.title: Canada invited to become first 'associate member' of the EU
items.summary: Canada was invited to become the EU's first 'associate member', with a proposed alliance covering technology, critical raw materials, energy and defence; details remain unclear.

items.title: UK to make ‘doxxing’ a criminal offense
items.summary: The UK will criminalise doxxing following a wave of online abuse directed at lifeboat volunteers, tightening rules on publishing personal data to harass.

items.title: Von der Leyen tries to stem tide on global threats ― from Trump to AI and climate
items.summary: Von der Leyen's State of the Union pushed European 'independence' against threats ranging from US policy to AI and climate, while floating associate membership for Canada.

items.title: EU wants Canada to become ‘associate member,’ von der Leyen says
items.summary: Von der Leyen proposed an 'Alliance for the Future' with Canada, building on the existing EU-Canada trade agreement alongside the associate membership offer.

items.title: 25 Years of Mass Surveillance Is Enough
items.summary: Essay by Bruce Schneier and Cindy Cohn arguing the post-9/11 shift from targeted surveillance to mass surveillance should end, 25 years on.
